purpose: M2 database credential lookup foundation; no HTTP authentication, token issuer, upload service, deployment or performance claim.

beforeAfter.before: The harness applies storage migration 001 and asserts that neither api_credentials nor resolve_api_credential(bytea) exists. This is missing functionality, not an old deployed authorization vulnerability.
beforeAfter.after: Migration 002 resolves an active synthetic editor key to its stored tenant/project and read,ingest scopes; a membership downgrade returns read, revocation returns zero rows, membership removal/rejoin does not resurrect the key.

manualReview.scope: SQL role/grant separation, forced row policies, fixed definer search path, finite statement-time expiry, current-role intersection, membership removal, digest bounds, reapply rollback, and docs claims. No independent specialized security review is claimed.

limitations: Stored SHA-256 digests must come from high-entropy random API secrets, not passwords. Generation, format, hashing/parsing and issuance are next slices.
HTTP routes must require returned identity and operation scope and use only its stored tenant/project; no route is implemented here.
Authorization uses statement snapshots; revocation does not cancel already-authorized requests.
Membership applies to all tenant projects; no per-project member assignments exist.
Migration owner is trusted and remains separate from runtime logins. Never grant auth_owner to a runtime login.
No public schema/root package export or runtime dependency changed. Portable operation remains database-free; M2 is open.
